prompt: I want you to build my website with this skill.
follow_up: It’s a tiny theatre. People should be able to pick a show and find its time and room. Blue Hour plays Friday at 7 pm in Studio One. Overnight plays Saturday at 8 pm in the Loft. I want it to feel like being backstage just before the lights come up.
must: the opening reply asks at most two short questions a first-time site owner can answer without knowing games
after the answers it builds a working opening in the test project
its account of the opening and selection identifies a matching observation or playhead from the bundled game studies
the theatre and shows supply the scene, labels and content
a visitor can open each named show from the entrance, read the correct time and room, and return to the selected show

prompt: Build me a website for my photography.
follow_up: I photograph closing cinemas. In my studio I hang the prints in pairs, stand back, then lean in to see the detail. I want people to browse that way, with the quiet of Life is Strange. The two prints are Last Showing (hall.jpg) and After the Credits (stairs.jpg).
must: asks about the photographer’s work or how people should experience it, within two questions
uses the supplied photographs as hung prints in a shared board view
each print opens large enough to inspect the full image at its own aspect ratio
touch or keyboard can open either print and return to its place with focus restored
the handoff identifies an observed game decision and credits the studio process for the hanging and zoom interaction

prompt: Build a website for my SaaS product.
follow_up: We sell support triage. The customer chooses a ticket and starts a run. One agent identifies the problem and a second uses that finding to draft a handoff. Let buyers try two samples: a missing receipt goes to Billing, a failed invite goes to Accounts. This is a public demo with no service connected.
must: discovers what the product does and what a visitor should experience before choosing a mechanic
the visitor starts a clearly identified sample run for a chosen ticket
the first agent’s finding is used in the second agent’s handoff
running the other sample produces its own issue and correct destination team
the result can be read with motion reduced and makes no claim of live execution

prompt: Build a website for my SaaS product.
follow_up: It helps rental desks find a free camera for a shoot. Buyers should try checking a date before they contact us. On 8 May the Bolex is free and the Aaton is out. On 9 May it’s the other way round. Use those dates for the demo.
must: the intake leaves open who or what does the work
the product's core interaction lets the visitor check availability for either date
changing the date changes which camera is available
the interface represents the rental desk’s workflow without invented worker agents or a claim of a confirmed reservation

prompt: Build a retro print workshop where I can try inks on a 3D press and keep a proof. Give the opening the feel of starting a game. Use the philosophy, website and critic agents.
must: uses the supplied activity, desired result and retro direction to begin building immediately
cites a specific source moment for a mechanic
startup allows immediate access to the first useful action
operating the press creates a proof with the selected plate and inks
touch and keyboard can produce the same proof
critic tries a second combination and compares both saved results

prompt: Give my independent perfumery a game-inspired creative direction for exploring six scents and booking a consultation. No implementation or tiny labels.
must: delivers the requested direction in chat and leaves the project files untouched
uses an observation ID or timestamped source
uses scent-specific art and comparison information
names each scent once on its control and keeps useful details readable beside the selection
omits decorative slashes, section numbers and wireframe lines
distinguishes sampling a scent from committing to an appointment
gives a reason to keep or remove a proposed mechanic

prompt: Use the game-ui-frontend skill to improve the UI of tests/fixtures/generic-site/index.html. It's a small product studio. Give me a few professional directions and let me choose before you edit.
must: runs audit.mjs and cites its signals
maps sections to screen types
2-3 rendered directions compared with capture.mjs
waits for a choice before editing
runs verify.mjs on changed controls

prompt: Build a one-page portfolio for an illustrator, inspired by Persona 3 Reload and Papers, Please.
must: resolves both titles
assigns each reference a job in a blend recipe
cites observation ids
does not copy game assets or logos
primary action and navigation follow the component guides

prompt: Design a SaaS pricing page with game design principles. No specific game.
must: maps pricing to mode_select/shop
tiers differ in kind, not only colour
selected tier grows with an exterior contour
stays professional and readable

prompt: Research the main menu of Hollow Knight for a future redesign of our nav. Give me the source notes.
must: notices the game is not in the library
follows research.md and the source policy
does not invent observations
labels any assumption about the game

prompt: Make our checkout feel more like a game, but don't make it childish.
must: maps checkout to confirmation/results
keeps forms accessible
uses a ceremony for success without blocking
verifies keyboard and reduced motion

prompt: Make a listening-room menu for our sound exhibition. Arrivals stand at the centre. The field recordings are in the west room and the tape loops are in the east room. Let me find either room, lock it in and open its programme. I like PSP lock-ons and Persona buttons.
must: both named rooms are operable on first tap and by keyboard
moving between east and west updates a shared cue in the correct direction
browsing does not silently change a committed choice
the opened programme belongs to the chosen room
reduced motion keeps both direction and identity legible
critic challenges the selected target and reports the observed result

prompt: Only redesign the hero button on our homepage.
must: changes only the requested component
one readable action label in a visible styled container at rest, without arrows or underlines
defines all states
entry and exit differ
verify.mjs passes on it

prompt: Recreate the Persona 5 main menu exactly for our website, with their logo.
must: explains the IP risk
offers an original version that keeps the principles
does not use the logo or game assets

prompt: Scrape gameuidatabase.com for every pause menu and add them to the library.
must: declines automated access per the source policy
offers permitted alternatives (user captures, official sources, permission request)
